title: Implications of the Fed’s Structural Shift
summary: Reserve normalization, emerging-market opportunities and metal caution.
assessment: Funding conditions improved as expected, and the yuan direction was right. Bitcoin and India floor calls failed. The Terra recap correctly highlights a prescient risk warning but omits an earlier relative-bullish stance. The December metal caution was timely, while the bank Treasury-holdings explanation conflates agencies with sovereign debt.

claims.claim: Funding pressure should ease.
claims.reason: The SOFR-IORB spread averaged +7.64 basis points before the December shift, +0.77 in Q1 2026 and -2.17 in April-October. Treasury-collateral overnight repo usage also declined on average; that series excludes agency collateral and is not total facility usage. Calendar spikes persisted, so “settle down” fits better than a claim of permanently zero facility use.

evidence.finding: Daily common-date spread to IORB: November 1-December 9 +7.64bp; Q1 +0.77bp; April-October -2.17bp.

claims.claim: Fed balance-sheet expansion has begun.
claims.reason: Purchases began December 12. The report explicitly acknowledges that its latest 2026 timing expectation was late, while the older 2024 scenario anticipated 2025. The policy sequence is verified; these revisions belong to one episode, not multiple independent wins.

evidence.title: Reserve management purchase announcement
evidence.finding: Purchases began December 12, 2025 to maintain ample reserves; initial monthly amount about $40 billion. Technical reserve supply does not itself establish a change in the interest-rate stance.

evidence.title: Early experience with reserve management purchases
evidence.finding: The Desk purchased about $40 billion monthly ahead of expected April tax flows. The objective was maintaining ample reserves.

claims.claim: The balance sheet reaches roughly $7 trillion.
claims.reason: The December 2026 endpoint remains in the future. Fed assets rose from $6.557 trillion on December 17, 2025 to $6.748 trillion on November 4, 2026. The arithmetic is a scenario, not a guaranteed minimum: purchases respond to reserve demand and other liabilities, not a binding 20%-of-GDP rule.

claims.claim: Deficits and purchases reinforce nominal growth.
claims.reason: Reserve creation can support settlement and funding, but reserve-management purchases do not mechanically expand bank lending or nominal GDP. A self-reinforcing fiscal causal loop needs evidence on fiscal impulse, credit demand, rates and counterfactual policy. Calling the baseline a minimum overstates what official projections commit to.

claims.reason: Circular leverage is a real risk mechanism, but “99%” has no specified universe or measurement rule. “Destined toward zero” also lacks a deadline. A successful Terra diagnosis cannot establish this claim for every unrelated protocol; stablecoins and tokenized assets are explicitly treated as exceptions.

claims.claim: Broad money matters more than reserves.
claims.reason: The distinction between reserve balances and deposit money is useful. But comparing Fed purchase size with total equity market capitalization does not establish a small price effect: marginal discount rates and expected policy can move valuations without a matching cash inflow. Neither money aggregate alone determines returns.

claims.claim: Fiat systems replace defaults with dilution.
claims.reason: A flexible monetary base can reduce some liquidity-driven defaults, but private and sovereign defaults still occur under fiat systems. Price levels depend on money demand, output and policy. The contrast describes a tendency, not an accounting identity or a guarantee that nominal IOUs always grow.

claims.claim: Banks hold over $4 trillion of Treasuries.
claims.reason: The contemporaneous H.8 category was Treasury AND agency securities, about $4.65 trillion. Roughly $2.70 trillion of it was mortgage-backed securities; even all non-MBS holdings were only about $1.95 trillion. Treating the whole category as Treasury debt overstates direct sovereign interest income.

claims.claim: More reserves increase banks’ interest income.
claims.reason: At a fixed positive IORB, more reserves raise gross interest income, but reserve supply also depends on currency, TGA and other liabilities. Net profit depends on deposit funding costs and forgone alternative assets. Asset and deposit growth is not automatically shareholder-value creation.

claims.claim: Dollar weakness eases emerging-market debt burdens.
claims.reason: For an unhedged borrower earning local currency and owing fixed dollars, dollar depreciation lowers the local-currency debt burden. Export revenues, hedges and local borrowing can offset or reverse exposure. A weaker exchange rate is not itself proof of abundant funding everywhere.

framework_lessons: Preserve the complete original thesis when evaluating retrospective success stories.
Separate a failed near-term floor from a still-open multi-year investment case.
verification_limitations: Current page snapshot is not an authenticated publication-date version.
A missing horizon is not replaced with an invented author deadline.
Market sensitivities use vendor adjusted closes and do not reconstruct portfolio execution.
